note.note:
Subjective:
- Current issues/reasons for visit:
  - Sore throat and dry cough for ~1 week.
  - Mild shortness of breath began ~3–4 days ago.
  - Seeks reassurance, symptomatic treatment, and a sick note for work.
- History of presenting complaints:
  - Sequence: Sore throat (Thu/Fri last week) → dry cough 1–2 days later → mild exertional breathlessness 3–4 days ago.
  - Cough: Dry; not worse at night; no sputum; no hemoptysis.
  - Associated symptoms: Intermittent headaches; felt feverish first ~3 days (now resolved); reports wheeze; reports chest pain (see conflict noted); decreased appetite without perceived weight loss; no nasal congestion; denies neck lumps on self-check; no rashes.
  - Functional impact: Missed work 2 days this week; earlier stated 3–4 days off due to illness (conflict noted).
  - Course: Fluctuating—periods of feeling better then worse.
  - Breathlessness: With walking/exertion; has not prevented usual activities/exercise.
- Past medical history:
  - Denies chronic conditions.
  - No asthma.
  - No personal or family history of clots (DVT/PE).
  - Family history: Mother with lung cancer.
- Medications:
  - None currently.
- Social history:
  - Non-smoker (rare experimentation only); no known asbestos exposure.
  - Lives in the UK; born in the US; recent travel only within Europe.
  - Employed; requested sick note.
- Allergies:
  - Peanuts. Denies medication allergies.

Objective:
- No vitals recorded.
- No in-person physical exam performed (telemedicine).
- Patient reports no palpable neck lumps on self-check.
- No investigations performed.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute sore throat with dry cough and mild exertional shortness of breath:
   - Assessment: Likely self-limiting viral illness (“cold”) per clinician reassurance.
   - Differential diagnosis: Serious causes (tuberculosis, lung cancer) considered unlikely if symptoms continue to improve.
   - Investigations planned: None ordered during this consult.
   - Treatment planned:
     - Paracetamol — dose/route/frequency not documented.
     - Encourage rest and increased oral fluids.
   - Safety-netting:
     - Seek in-person GP assessment urgently if breathlessness worsens, sudden change in breathing occurs, or new concerning symptoms develop.
     - If not improving within 4–5 days, re-contact a medical professional for reassessment.

2. Concern about serious causes (tuberculosis, lung cancer):
   - Assessment: Reassurance provided; not currently suspected given clinical course and expected improvement.
   - Plan: Monitor symptoms; follow up if not improving or if red flags develop.

3. Work accommodation (sick note request):
   - Assessment: Work absence due to illness.
   - Treatment/Plan: Sick note provided for a few more days off work — specific duration not documented.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements:
  - Vitals (temperature, heart rate, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation).
  - Physical exam (throat/oropharynx, chest/respiratory exam).
  - Medication dosing instructions for paracetamol.
  - Documentation of current over-the-counter remedies used, if any.
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - Shortness of breath: initially denied, later affirmed — conflict noted.
  - Chest pain: patient reported “a bit,” later clinician phrased as no chest pain — conflict noted.
  - Work absence: stated “3–4 days” off vs. “2 days this week” — conflict noted.
  - Date of birth given would indicate a child, which conflicts with being employed — conflict noted.
- Transcript quality:
  - Some interruptions/over-talking and minor ambiguities; end of consult was rushed, limiting detail on exam and plan specifics.
